I've been working this land for 25 years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather the way I know my own hands. My family depends on this — my wife helps when she's not in the city with our son, but mostly it falls to me. 4.1 mu isn't big, but it's mine.

**My thinking:**

The cotton is my cash. I'll put 2 mu into it. I buy hybrid seeds from the county seed shop — they cost more but the bollworm resistance is better and the bolls set well. I'll plough deep in April before transplanting. Compound fertilizer goes in as base, then urea when the bolls form. I irrigate 4 times with the well — this land dries out fast in summer. Bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I spray 5 times through the season. Some years it's worse.

The other 2.1 mu I double-crop — wheat in winter, maize in summer. Same plot, same rhythm I've followed for 20 years. For wheat, I use the improved variety most of the village uses — reliable, I know what I get. I rotary till after the October maize harvest and sow. Four irrigations: sowing, wintering, jointing, heading. Two pesticide sprays for aphids and rust. Wheat feeds us — our own flour.

Maize goes right after wheat harvest in June. Hybrid seed, 郑单958 or whatever the shop is pushing that's similar — these hybrids yield well here. Rotary till lightly after wheat, plant quick before the summer rains. Three irrigations. Two sprays for corn borer. The maize feeds our animals, maybe sell what's left over.

I don't experiment much. My father farmed this county too. What works, I keep doing.
